summary: Verified the scroll-restoration bug fix in PageShell (useEffect calling window.scrollTo on location.pathname change). Executed all 6 requested scroll-position scenarios via Playwright on the public preview URL. All navigations from a scrolled-down state land the new route at window.scrollY = 0.

test_results.case: /contact(Y=810) -> / via footer-link-agencies (immediate=811 due to same-page jump, settles to 0)

critical_code_review_comments: PageShell scroll-to-top useEffect at App.js:143-144 is correct and minimal.
Line 131 (footer-link-contact) redundantly calls window.scrollTo after navigate('/contact') — PageShell already handles this; the extra call is harmless but duplicative.
App.js is a large monolithic file (>300 lines with all routes/components). Consider splitting into modules for maintainability (not blocking).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Scroll-restoration verified across /, /work, /work/:slug, /agency/:slug, /contact. Fix is a single useEffect in PageShell keyed on location.pathname using window.scrollTo({top:0,behavior:'instant'}).
rca of the issue: React Router v6 does not restore scroll on route change; new routes inherited the previous page's scrollY. Fix: PageShell subscribes to useLocation and imperatively scrolls the window to (0,0) on pathname change. Verified: all 6 tested navigations from bottom/middle scroll positions now open the new route at Y=0.
